<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. VIII.|ACCORDING TO S. LVKE.|159}}</noinclude>forth, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=3}}† and Ioane the vvife of Chusa Herods procurator, and Susan, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''aliæ multæ''}}∷ many others {{sup|‖}} that did minister vnto him of their substance.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=4}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 13, 1. Mr. 4, 1.''}}* And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the Sunday of Sexagesme.}}vvhen a very great multitude assembled, and hastened out of the cities vnto him, he said by a similitude. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=5}}† The sovver vvent forth to sovv his seede. and vvhiles he sovveth, some fel by the vvay side, and vvas troden vpon, and the foules of the aire did eate it. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=6}}† And other some fel vpon the rocke: and being shot vp, it withered, because it had not moisture. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=7}}† And othersome fel among thornes, and the thornes grovving vp vvithal, choked it. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=8}}† And other some fel vpon good ground: and being shot vp, yelded fruite an hundred fold. Saying these things he cried, He that hath eares to heare, let him heare.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=9}}† And his disciples asked him vvhat this parable was. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=10}}† To vvhom he said, To you it is giuen to knovv the mysterie of the kingdom of God, but to the rest in parables, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 6, 9.''}}* that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ See the Annotations vpon S. Matthew. c. 13, 14.}}∷ seeing they may not see, and hearing may not vnderstand. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=11}}† And the parable is this: The seede, is the vvord of God. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=12}}† And they besides the vvay: are those that heare, then the deuil commeth, and taketh the vvord out of their hart, lest beleeuing they be saued. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=13}}† For they vpon the rocke: such as vvhen they heare, vvith ioy receiue the vvord: and these haue no rootes: because {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Against the Heretikes that say, faith once had can not be lost, and that he which now hath not faith, neuer had.}}∷ for a time they beleeue, and in time of tentation they reuolt. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=14}}† And that vvhich fel into thornes, are they that haue heard, and going their vvaies, are choked vvith cares and riches and pleasures of this life, and render not fruite. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15}}† And that vpon good ground: are they vvhich in a good and very good hart, hearing the vvord, doe reteine it, and yeld fruite in patience.⊣

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=16}}† And no man lighting a candel doth couer it vvith a vessel, or put it vnder a bed: but setteth it vpon a candelsticke, that they that enter in, may see the light. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=17}}† For there is not any thing secrete, that shal not be made manifest: nor hid, that shal not be knowen, & come abrode. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=18}}† See therfore how you heare. For he that hath, to him shal be giuen: and vvhosoeuer hath not, that also vvhich he thinketh he hath, shal be taken avvay from him.

{{verse|chapter=8|verse=19}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 46. Mr. 3, 31.''}}* his mother and brethren came vnto him: and they could not come at him for the multitude. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=20}}† And it vvas told him, Thy mother and {{sup|‖}} thy brethren stand vvithout, desirous to see thee. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=21}}† Who ansvvering said to them, My {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He did not here disdainfully speake of his mother, but teacheth that our spiritual kinred is to be preferred before carnal cognation. ''Hilar. in 12 Mat''.}}∷ mother and<noinclude>{{rh|||my}}</noinclude>
